scope: A lighter picture on the headset PC, so a headset's full panel resolution fits lighter headset PCs: the one-pass frame shader with its foveation terms worked out once per frame, each eye a layer of workgroups and every constant in a uniform buffer (one shader for every GPU); the pixels the lenses never show skipped (the visible-area mesh and the lens distortion's outline, with a margin; the mesh's way up checked against the outline, or both ways up without one); each eye shown at 90 % or 80 % of its size while the headset PC's GPU holds the stream below refresh, instead of SteamVR halving the frame rate; GPU time stamps around the pass and the plane copy; the Beyond's 2560 size called Native. Every package carries version 1.0.0.11; the host's driver is 1.0.0.9's, unchanged.
changes: client/platform/linux/fused.comp: the per-frame constants from a std140 uniform buffer (binding 3) and the visible spans from a storage buffer (binding 4); one square root and one reciprocal per axis instead of the inverse's divisions; each eye a workgroup layer (gl_WorkGroupID.z); no push constants (fused-uniform.spv removed)
client/device/conversion.hpp: FusedAxis, FusedEye, FusedFrame (544 bytes), fusedAxis and fusedFrameConstants (double precision), scaledEyeSize

client/device/visible_area.hpp (new): per-row spans from the visible-area mesh and the distortion outline, the margin, the share, and alignMeshes (the mesh's orientation checked against the outline, or both orientations used without one); openvr_device.cpp visibleArea (GetHiddenAreaMesh inverse, ComputeDistortion along the panel's edge)

client/platform/linux/vulkan.cpp and video.hpp: a uniform and a storage buffer per output image, the spans per size, each image cleared once (and again after the re-aim pass or new spans), timestamp queries around the pass and the decode-time copy, both written at the bottom of the pipe (also client/platform/windows/vulkan_upload.cpp), STATUS Lens area (pixels skipped only where the fused pass runs), VISIBLE_AREA and GPU time stamp lines
client/platform/linux/main.cpp and decoder.cpp: --full-frame, --scale N and the stdin command scale N; frame_pass_gpu, plane_copy_gpu, shown_scale, shown_eye_width and visible_share on TIMING

launcher/output_scale.py (new) and launcher/app.py: the shown size stepped to 90 % and 80 % while the GPU holds the stream below refresh (seconds with SteamVR's GPU time only), back up when there is room, the wait before a step up doubled after one undone within 5 minutes, pinned after one undone within 30 s or after three round trips; the size chosen and sent under one lock with the switch; SCALE lines; the settings lens_area and keep_frame_rate; launcher/timeline.py, desktop.html, game_ui.py; launcher/headset.py: Native

tests: tests/test_vrostbridge_1011.py, tests/visible_area_tests.cpp, tests/video_pass_tests.cpp with tests/openvr_stand_in.hpp (written by tests/make_openvr_stand_in.py), new sections in tests/fused_shader_tests.cpp, tests/shown_size_tests.cpp and tests/planar_upload_tests.cpp; earlier release tests made to accept later releases
Version 1.0.0.11 on every package; documents, release notes and the two PDFs

host.driver: 1.0.0.9's, byte for byte: ALVR f5023f8e with patches 0001 to 0023 (no patch changed)

toolchain: As 1.0.0.10: Ubuntu 24.04.5, GCC 13.3.0, CMake 3.28.3 + Ninja 1.11.1 (Linux client); clang-cl/lld-link/llvm-lib/llvm-rc 19.1.1 + xwin Windows SDK and CRT (Windows client and launchers); PyInstaller 6.22.3 / Python 3.12.3; NSIS 3.09; ReportLab (PDFs) with mermaid-cli in Chromium; Wine 9.0 with Mesa lavapipe; Node 22 (page checks); PowerShell 7.4.6 (script parse); the Khronos Vulkan validation layer 1.3.275. The driver, both transports and FFmpeg's DLLs are 1.0.0.9's builds, not rebuilt: their sources are unchanged.
frame_pass_cost_estimate: RADV's compiler statistics (ACO, VK_KHR_pipeline_executable_properties, null devices of the integrated Radeon generations of handheld PCs), per path with the region and detail forced: VALU instructions per pixel 232 -> 150 (reduced periphery), 254 -> 198 (sharp centre), 336 -> 252 (blend band); inverse-throughput estimate down 34-40 %; VGPRs 48 -> 32. Not a measurement on a real GPU: the reports' frame_pass_gpu will be.

tests.native_linux: CTest: 100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 28, on the final source; installed again, the native files came out byte-identical to the packaged ones
tests.native_windows_under_wine: CTest: 100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 27, on the final source, video_pass_contracts (the client's own frame path with CPU-decoded frames through its upload) included; the folder it installed is the one packaged.
tests.frame_path: video_pass_contracts runs VulkanVideo itself, from decoded planes to the image SteamVR is given, against a stand-in SteamVR generated from the OpenVR headers, on lavapipe (on Linux the planes are filled as the VA-API copy fills them; the VA-API import itself does not run here): a flat colour within 0.11 levels, a pattern pixel for pixel in both eyes, a foveated ramp within 0.72 levels of where ALVR's inverse puts each pixel, the lens spans (skipped pixels black, the rest unchanged), an image the re-aim pass filled cleared again, a 90 % output with its own spans, a faulty lens area ignored, and the pass's and the copy's GPU time read back. It fails when the re-aim pass stops marking its image for a clear.
tests.vulkan_validation: The Khronos validation layer with synchronisation validation over every Vulkan test on Linux (6 tests, no messages) and over video_pass_tests.exe under Wine (no messages); it had flagged a test-only readback offset in tests/planar_upload_tests.cpp, since aligned. A barrier after the clear removed on purpose was reported as SYNC-HAZARD-WRITE-AFTER-WRITE.
tests.rust_and_driver: not run again: patches/ and client/transport/ are unchanged since 1.0.0.10 (git diff), so the driver and both transports are 1.0.0.9's builds and 1.0.0.9's results stand (alvr_sockets 18 and alvr_audio 11 passed, the driver modules 21)
tests.pages: tests/test_desktop_ui.js in Node: Desktop connection workflow smoke checks passed.
tests.python: Ran 1445 tests, OK, 1 skipped (tests/test_vrostbridge_1011.py: 26 of its own); the one skipped, test_windows_packaging's build of both launchers, needs clang, lld-link, llvm-rc and the Windows SDK and passed when run with them

independent_review.what: A separate review of the changes against 1.0.0.10 (46f9ef0), with its own build and test run (CTest 28/28, Python 1440 OK), the Khronos validation layer with synchronisation validation, and 1.0.0.10's shader test built for a comparison. No blocker: no crash, hang, Vulkan misuse, wrong picture or loss of precision found. Its own checks: the per-frame constants against the inverse with random edge ratios 1.5 to 8 (at most 5.8e-4 texel, against 0.19 for 1.0.0.10's per-pixel terms), 1.36 million visible pixel centres from random meshes and outlines (none outside the spans), the uniform buffer's std140 layout by reflection.
fixed_before_packaging: the output scale could swing back and forth (36 size changes in 30 minutes in the review's simulation of a PC that falls behind 40 s after each return): a step up undone within 5 minutes now doubles the wait before the next, and the third such return pins the size (7 changes, then 90 %, in the same simulation)
the seconds while a step settles counted towards the next step down; they no longer do
a throttled second without SteamVR's GPU time counted as behind; it no longer does (the documents said so)

turning Keep the frame rate off could be overtaken by a size chosen just before; choosing and sending now happen under one lock that the switch also takes (tested from a second thread), and a size not sent is queued again
STATUS Lens area said pixels were skipped also without the fused pass
the begin time stamps were written at the top of the pipe and could include the tail of earlier work; both stamps are now written at the bottom of the pipe
a mesh without an outline (an unconfirmed suspicion) is now used both ways up, so an upside-down mesh cannot hide what the lenses show
five statements in the documents that said more than the tests show
left_as_is: a change of size makes the output images anew, one per shown frame, which may cost a refresh; the back-off keeps such changes rare
edge ratios between 1.0001 and 1.01, which no setting gives (the choices are 2 to 5), place a texel up to 0.75 off, against 0.39 in 1.0.0.10
